messages:
jordan: FYI pushed PR #2131 - reduces token cost by ~18% for streaming workloads. can someone eyeball the caching + quant changes before i merge? trying to get this in today's merge window. :clock1:

jordan: summary: lower cache_ttl for short seqs, enable int8 quant path for decoder, add routing fallback to cpu for cold starts. perf/localbench numbers below.

jordan: perf quick snapshot (microbench):
```
before: p95=120ms, tokens/sec=640, cost/unit=$0.012
after:  p95=135ms, tokens/sec=710, cost/unit=$0.0098
delta: +12% latency p95, -18% cost/unit
```

taylor: @jordan thanks — can you paste the exact config diff? curious where the latency hit is coming from. also, did you run long-seq tests (>2048)?

jordan: sure, excerpt from the PR:
```yaml
inference:
  cache:
    prefix_ttl_ms: 12000  # was 30000 for long-run workloads
  quantization:
    enabled: true
    dtype: int8
routing:
  fallback_on_capacity: cpu
  preferred_gpu_types: [a100, h100]
```

jordan: long-seq was run on the canary nodes - saw p95 jump on sequences >2k, but avg tokens/sec improved for 512-1024 common requests.

sam: i'll take a quick pass in ~30. main question is rollback plan if this spikes latencies in prod. also let's make sure telemetry flags capture prefix cache hits.

alex: +1 on capturing cache-hit metrics. also please add an automated canary that ramps traffic over 10m with CPU fallback enabled. if CI is green i can approve during the merge window.

morgan: skimmed the diff — looks ok but we should gate int8 on model compatibility list. some older ops fallback to fp16 and cause extra kernel launches. add a feature-flag.

ci-bot: CI: all checks passed for PR #2131 (build, unit-tests, e2e-smoke).

taylor: ran a quick static review — one nit in the routing comparator (use stable sort to avoid nondeterministic route order). i filed a tiny change request on the PR.

jordan: thanks — pushed fix for stable sort and added telemetry for cache_hit_rate + prefix_evictions. new commit sha: b7f3c2a. updated canary ramp to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 20m per alex request.

morgan: assuming telemetry looks good in canary i'm fine with approval. :thumbsup:

sam: will watch the canary dashboard for the next hour and ping if anything looks off.

jordan: cool — merging into staging after 10m unless anyone objects. TY all :pray:
